He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]], and was drafted second overall in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the Spurs. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class. His father is former NBA player [[Ron Harper]]. ==Early life and high school career== Dylan Robert Harper was born on March 2, 2006 in [[Englewood, New Jersey]], at the [[Englewood Hospital and Medical Center|Englewood Hospital]].{{Cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Kevin |date=2023-12-08 |title=Dylan Harper wants to be the NBA's No. 1 pick. Can Rutgers get him there? |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2023/12/staying-power.html |access-date=2026-05-29 |website=nj |language=en}} Harper grew up in [[Franklin Lakes, New Jersey]] and attended [[Don Bosco Preparatory High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2023/01/11/dylan-harper-top-nj-basketball-recruit-don-bosco/69766435007/|title=Considered a top High School basketball talent in NJ, Dylan Harper does it all on and off the court|work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|first=Greg|last=Mattura|date=January 11, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}} He averaged 15.2 points per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://indiana.rivals.com/news/indiana-extends-offer-to-top-50-2024-guard-dylan-harper|title=Indiana extends offer to top-50 2024 guard Dylan Harper|first=Alec|last=Lasley|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=July 19, 2023}} Harper was named the Boys Basketball Player of the Year by ''[[NJ.com]]'' as a junior after averaging 24.9 points, 6.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 2.0 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Yc3gUeKu3USlr-fe-ECyyg/high-school-basketball-could-dylan-harper-have-a-better-nba-career-than-his-father-ron-harper.htm|title=High school basketball: Could Dylan Harper have a better NBA career than his father Ron Harper?|first=Jordan|last=Divens|website=[[MaxPreps]]|date=May 24, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2023/03/don-bosco-preps-dylan-harper-is-the-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-2022-23.html|title=Don Bosco Prep's Dylan Harper is the Boys Basketball Player of the Year, 2022–23|first=Brandon|last=Gould|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=March 20, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} Harper averaged 22.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game while leading the Ironmen to a 29–3 record and a NJSIAA Non-Public A state championship during his senior season. Harper played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball for the New York Renaissance.{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2022/07/nj-star-dylan-harper-leads-ny-rens-into-peach-jam-semis-says-rutgers-is-recruiting-him-the-hardest.html|title=N.J. star Dylan Harper leads NY Rens into Peach Jam semis, says Rutgers is recruiting him the hardest|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=July 22, 2022|access-date=March 2, 2023}} He also played in the 2023 USA Basketball Men’s Junior National Team minicamp in Colorado Springs.{{cite web|url=https://andscape.com/features/rookie-guard-dylan-harper-ready-for-nba-education-with-san-antonio-spurs/|title=Rookie guard Dylan Harper ready for NBA education with San Antonio Spurs|first=Marc|last=Spears|website=[[Andscape]]|date=July 9, 2025|access-date=July 11, 2025}} ===Recruiting=== Harper was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2023/07/at-nike-peach-jam-rutgers-remains-laser-focused-on-no-1-target-dylan-harper.html|title=At Nike Peach Jam, Rutgers remains laser-focused on No. 1 target Dylan Harper|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} He was rated the number one overall recruit for the class of 2024 by ''[[ESPN]]'' during the summer before the start of his senior year.{{cite [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], his brother‘s alma mater, over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Indiana ===San Antonio Spurs (2025–present)=== ====All-Rookie honors and First Finals Appearance (2025–2026)==== Harper was selected with the second overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-select-dylan-harper-and-carter-bryant-in-the-first-round-of-2025-nba-draft|title=Spurs Select Dylan Harper and Carter Bryant in the First Round of 2025 NBA Draft|date=June 25, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 25, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45585461/spurs-land-rutgers-dylan-harper-no-2-pick-nba-draft|title=Spurs land Rutgers' Dylan Harper with No. 2 pick in NBA draft|website=ESPN.com|last=Wright|first=Michael|date=June 25, 2025|access-date=June 25, 2025}} Harper was later included in the 2025 [[NBA Summer League]] roster of the Spurs.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-announce-2025-summer-league-roster|title=Spurs Announce 2025 Summer League Roster|date=June 30, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 30, 2025}} On July 3, 2025, the Spurs announced that they signed Harper.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2025-second-overall-pick-dylan-harper|title=Spurs Sign 2025 Second Overall Pick Dylan Harper|date=July 3, 2025|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 3, 2025}} On October 22, Harper made his NBA debut, coming off the bench with fifteen points plus four rebounds and two assists in a 125–92 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=Wembanyama scores 40 as Spurs spoil Flagg debut with 125–92 rout of Mavericks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401809235|date=October 22, 2025|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2025}} On March 21, 2026, Harper scored a career-high 24 points in a 134–119 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-dylan-harper-career-high-24-points/|title=Spurs' Dylan Harper: Career-high 24 points|website=CBS Sports|date=March 21, 2026|access-date=March 22, 2026}} After the regular season, Harper was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{cite web |title=Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel headline 2025–26 Kia All-Rookie Teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-rookie-teams-announced |website=NBA.com |date=May 21, 2026 |access-date=May 21, 2026}} [[File:Dylan Harper in 2026 Western Conference Finals.jpg|thumb|Harper during the [[2026 NBA playoffs|2026 NBA Conference Finals]]]] On April 24, in Game 3 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(2) San Antonio Spurs vs. (7) Portland Trail Blazers|Western Conference First Round]] against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Harper put up 27 points and 10 rebounds in a 120–108 win. His teammate [[Stephon Castle]] put up 33 points, as they joined [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Russell Westbrook]] as the only duos to each put up 25 points in the same playoff game at 21 years old or younger in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-dylan-harper-stephon-castle-game-3-heroics-kd-westbrook|title=Spurs guards Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle’s Game 3 heroics join Kevin Durant, Russell Westbrook company|website=ClutchPoints|last=Davis|first=Josh|date=April 25, 2026|access-date=April 27, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7228272/2026/04/25/spurs-blazers-nba-playoffs-game-3-dylan-harper-carter-bryant/|title=Carter Bryant, Dylan Harper take over Spurs’ comeback win in moment they dreamed of|website=The Athletic|last=Weiss|first=Jared|date=April 25, 2026|access-date=April 27, 2026}} He also became the youngest player in NBA history to record at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in a conference finals game.{{cite web |title=Spurs-Thunder: Don't ignore what Dylan Harper is doing as a 20-year-old rookie in the playoffs |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/article/spurs-thunder-dont-ignore-what-dylan-harper-is-doing-as-a-20-year-old-rookie-in-the-playoffs-142833827.html |website=Yahoo Sports |date=May 20, 2026 |access-date=May 21, 2026}} On May 18, in Game 1 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(1) Oklahoma City Thunder vs. (2) San Antonio Spurs|Western Conference Finals]] against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Harper recorded 24 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and a franchise playoff-record seven steals in a 122–115 double-overtime victory.{{cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |title=San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper ‘all business’ on court in Western Conference finals |url=https://andscape.com/features/san-antonio-spurs-dylan-harper-playoffs-rookie-thunder-deaaron-fox-injury/ |website=Andscape |date=May 20, 2026 |access-date=May 21, 2026}} In the process, he became only the second rookie in NBA history to record at least 20 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and five steals in a playoff game, joining [[Magic Johnson]].{{cite web |title=Dylan Harper Had Historic Playoff Game for Spurs |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/san-antonio-spurs/dylan-harper-historic-playoff-game1-spurs/ |website=Heavy.com |date=May 20, 2026 |access-date=May 21, 2026}} In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Harper recorded a team-high 25 points along with five rebounds and four assists without committing a turnover in a 94–90 loss to the Knicks, as the Spurs lost the series 4–1.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-devin-vassell-lets-slip-dylan-harper-was-upset-with-playing-time-different-roles-in-rookie-season|title=Spurs’ Devin Vassell lets slip Dylan Harper was ‘upset with playing time, different roles’ in rookie season|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship, defeating Spurs in five games|website=nba.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}} In his first NBA Finals appearance, Harper averaged 18 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 3 assists per game. Despite appearing in all five games off the bench, he finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer in the series behind [[Victor Wembanyama]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.onthebanks.com/rutgers-basketball/53377/dylan-harper-shines-on-basketballs-biggest-stage-despite-spurs-finals-defeat|title=Dylan Harper Shines on Basketball’s Biggest Stage Despite Spurs’ Finals Defeat|website=SB Nation|last=Sarkar|first=Arnav|date=June 15, 2026|access-date=June 20, 2026}} ==National team career== Harper was named to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-19 basketball team]] to play in the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2023/06/don-bosco-star-rutgers-target-dylan-harper-earns-spot-on-usa-basketball-u19-fiba-world-cup-team.html|title=Don Bosco star, Rutgers target Dylan Harper earns spot on USA Basketball U19 FIBA World Cup team|first=Brian|last=Fonseca|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=June 16, 2023|access-date=June 19, 2023}} He averaged 9.3 points and 4.6 rebounds per game as Team USA finished fourth in the tournament.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/rutgers/Article/A-look-at-how-Dylan-Harper-fared-in-FIBA-U19-World-Cup-212384197/|title=A look at how Dylan
